notes: Official 2026 programme allocations, estimates, additional Budget measures and fiscal projections. Many rows overlap. Never sum selected rows or infer a sector residual.

programmes.title: State pension expenditure
programmes.description: Pensions form the largest social protection programme grouping, reflecting support for people reaching pension age and qualifying under State Pension rules. The Minister described spending as above €12 billion and just under 42% of the department's 2026 estimate.
programmes.limitation: This is a lower bound expressed in the source, not an exact €12bn expenditure return.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Illness, disability and carers' payments
programmes.description: This grouping supports people whose health or caring responsibilities affect income. It includes multiple social insurance and social assistance schemes, not one standard payment or an individual disability-services provider.
programmes.limitation: This is income-support programme spending and must not be merged with the separate specialist disability-services budget.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Working-age income supports
programmes.description: Working-age supports include jobseeker payments, lone-parent supports, maternity and paternity-related benefits and other qualifying income support. The official committee statement puts 2026 estimated spending at €4.45 billion.
programmes.limitation: The schemes have different eligibility rules. The total is not just spending on unemployment.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Employment support programmes
programmes.description: Employment supports help qualifying people move towards work, including schemes such as Community Employment, Tús and the Rural Social Scheme. The departmental presentation estimated €734 million for 2026.
programmes.limitation: This amount is separate from working-age cash payments and should not be equated with all employment policy expenditure.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Children and family payments
programmes.description: The children and families programme includes Child Benefit and other qualifying family payments. The Minister estimated €3.15 billion for 2026, nearly eleven per cent of the social protection budget.
programmes.limitation: Child Benefit is part of this figure, not an extra allocation to add on top.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Child Benefit
programmes.description: Child Benefit is a monthly cash transfer for eligible children. The Minister stated that more than €2.2 billion of the children-and-families programme would go to this payment in 2026.
programmes.limitation: The value is a lower bound and a component of the children-and-families programme; do not add them together.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Supplementary welfare and miscellaneous supports
programmes.description: The department's supplementary programme includes additional supports for qualifying households, with 2026 expenditure described as just over €1 billion at the February committee meeting.
programmes.limitation: A rounded lower bound, not the exact subhead total; particular schemes must be sourced separately.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Auto-enrolment programme funding
programmes.description: Ireland's new workplace auto-enrolment system receives a 2026 programme allocation for State top-ups and the authority's initial operational costs. The Minister said projected expenditure was just under €178 million.
programmes.limitation: This budget includes start-up costs and is not identical to State contributions paid into workers' accounts.
programmes.source_label: Dáil Select Committee, Vote 37 Revised Estimates, February 2026

programmes.title: Mental health services
programmes.description: The 2026 mental health allocation supports inpatient and community services, crisis support and staff expansion. The Minister described the envelope as almost €1.6 billion for mental health.
programmes.limitation: A rounded sector-within-sector funding announcement, not a report of mental health services already delivered.
programmes.source_label: Department of Health, Budget 2026 mental health announcement

programmes.title: Additional crisis and suicide-prevention funding
programmes.description: Additional 2026 money targets crisis support and suicide prevention, including expanded nursing, community crisis and specialist services. It is an incremental measure within mental health funding.
programmes.limitation: This is new funding, not the entire mental health budget or an additional amount to sum with it.
programmes.source_label: Department of Health, Budget 2026 mental health announcement

programmes.title: New specialist mental health teams
programmes.description: A €10 million Budget 2026 provision supports eight new specialist community mental health teams, including dedicated services for complex needs and clinical programmes.
programmes.limitation: This is a targeted new measure within the wider mental health allocation.
programmes.source_label: Department of Health, 2026 clinical programme allocation

programmes.title: HSE buildings and equipment capital
programmes.description: The HSE Building and Equipment Capital Plan funds buildings, equipment and health infrastructure, including capacity expansion. The published 2026 capital plan provides €1.327 billion.
programmes.limitation: This is a HSE capital plan envelope, not annual healthcare operating expenditure or the cost of a single hospital.
programmes.source_label: Department of Health, HSE Capital Plans 2026

programmes.title: HSE Digital for Care capital
programmes.description: The HSE Digital for Care capital plan provides €263 million for information and digital infrastructure in 2026, distinct from physical construction and equipment budgets.
programmes.limitation: This is a capital allocation and does not indicate the value of digital contracts awarded or delivered.
programmes.source_label: Department of Health, HSE Capital Plans 2026

programmes.title: Special education in schools
programmes.description: The education department confirmed about €3 billion was provided for special education in 2026. This supports additional teaching, SNAs and school settings for pupils with special educational needs.
programmes.limitation: This is a broad schools allocation. It does not determine a payment or funding figure for an individual child or school.
programmes.source_label: Minister for Education and Youth, 2026 special education statement

programmes.title: Education and youth capital investment
programmes.description: Budget 2026 earmarks €1.6 billion for the Department of Education and Youth under the 2026–2030 National Development Plan. It supports school capital investment and infrastructure priorities.
programmes.limitation: This is a department-wide capital envelope, not a verified sum for any one school or county.
programmes.source_label: Department of Education and Youth, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Additional school transport investment
programmes.description: Budget 2026 announced a €69 million investment to strengthen the school transport scheme, important for access to education in rural and other communities.
programmes.limitation: The announcement is a Budget measure; do not treat it as the entire annual school transport programme cost.
programmes.source_label: Department of Education and Youth, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Housing programme Exchequer funding
programmes.description: The 2026 housing programme includes €7.21 billion of Exchequer support across current and capital spending. The wider sector total also includes other local-government responsibilities.
programmes.limitation: This programme total is narrower than the full €11.4bn housing sector; other funding vehicles can increase the capital investment envelope.
programmes.source_label: Department of Housing, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Housing programme capital
programmes.description: Within the €7.21 billion housing programme, €5.19 billion is capital funding for housing investment. Non-Exchequer mechanisms can bring total housing capital investment above this figure.
programmes.limitation: This is already included in the €7.21bn housing programme, not additional public spending.
programmes.source_label: Department of Housing, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Housing programme current spending
programmes.description: Within the €7.21 billion housing programme, €2.02 billion is current spending on running and supporting relevant housing programmes rather than capital construction.
programmes.limitation: This is already included in the housing programme total; do not double-count it.
programmes.source_label: Department of Housing, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Homelessness services
programmes.description: Budget 2026 earmarked €563.5 million to support homelessness services, including funding delivered through housing authorities. The allocation is distinct from counting new homes completed.
programmes.limitation: The figure is an announced funding allocation, not an audited 2026 outturn or the total cost of homelessness to all public bodies.
programmes.source_label: Department of Housing, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Tenancies regulation and advocacy
programmes.description: The housing budget assigned €24 million to the Residential Tenancies Board and other advocacy services. These services provide regulation and support for renters and landlords.
programmes.limitation: The allocation includes other advocacy services; it should not be described as RTB-only operating expenditure.
programmes.source_label: Department of Housing, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Traveller accommodation support
programmes.description: The 2026 housing budget provides €34 million for Traveller-community supports, including accommodation, repairs and maintenance work.
programmes.limitation: This announcement describes a programme package and should not be interpreted as only new construction.
programmes.source_label: Department of Housing, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Department of Transport capital envelope
programmes.description: The Department of Transport announced €3.43 billion in capital funding for 2026, supporting long-term transport infrastructure such as roads, public transport and active travel.
programmes.limitation: Individual project figures can span multiple years and must be verified separately rather than subtracted from this one-year envelope.
programmes.source_label: Department of Transport, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Department of Transport current envelope
programmes.description: The Department of Transport announced €1.31 billion in current funding for 2026, including road services, public transport operations and wider transport responsibilities.
programmes.limitation: Current spending is separate from capital investment, and the headline is not the same as fare subsidies alone.
programmes.source_label: Department of Transport, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Public transport PSO services
programmes.description: A €940 million Public Service Obligation allocation helps subsidise bus and rail services and sustain access to public transport across Ireland.
programmes.limitation: This is a funding allocation to services, not a forecast of passenger numbers or a direct subsidy for an individual user.
programmes.source_label: Department of Transport, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Road networks and road safety
programmes.description: The transport budget announced €1.72 billion for national, regional and local roads and road safety. Work ranges from maintenance and improvement to infrastructure projects.
programmes.limitation: Road and safety funding can include current and capital components, so it overlaps departmental envelopes and cannot be added to them.
programmes.source_label: Department of Transport, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Active travel and greenways
programmes.description: The government allocated €360 million for walking, cycling and greenway projects in 2026. Project and county allocations are published separately and can be tracked against this programme.
programmes.limitation: This capital programme falls within wider transport investment, so avoid adding it on top of the transport capital total.
programmes.source_label: Department of Transport, 2026 active travel

programmes.title: NTA walking and cycling allocation
programmes.description: Of the wider active-travel programme, the National Transport Authority was allocated €290 million for cycling and walking infrastructure across Irish towns, villages and cities.
programmes.limitation: This is part of the €360m active-travel envelope, not a second allocation to add to the total.
programmes.source_label: National Transport Authority, 2026 active travel allocations

programmes.title: National roads Exchequer capital
programmes.description: Transport Infrastructure Ireland's 2026 national roads capital allocation covers improvements, protection and renewal of the national road network.
programmes.limitation: The figure is part of road funding and capital expenditure; it must not be stacked on top of both parent allocations.
programmes.source_label: Department of Transport, 2026 roads announcement

programmes.title: National roads PPP payments
programmes.description: The national roads funding announcement included €104 million for public-private partnership arrangements associated with national roads.
programmes.limitation: This is a component of national road funding, not a new or independent major-road construction budget.
programmes.source_label: Department of Transport, 2026 roads announcement

programmes.title: Justice sector capital allocation
programmes.description: The 2026 justice-sector capital plan provides €390 million across Garda, prisons, courts, the Justice department and other listed votes.
programmes.limitation: Capital is a subset of broader justice spending; these allocations should not be treated as all policing and justice costs.
programmes.source_label: Department of Justice, 2026–2030 capital plan

programmes.title: Garda capital expenditure
programmes.description: The Garda capital ceiling provides €173.8 million for property, vehicles, equipment and technology programmes in 2026.
programmes.limitation: This is one component of the €390m justice capital envelope, not the overall Garda budget.
programmes.source_label: Department of Justice, 2026–2030 capital plan

programmes.title: Prison capital programme
programmes.description: The justice investment plan allocates €67.9 million to Irish Prison Service capital investment for 2026.
programmes.limitation: This is a capital envelope, not day-to-day prison operating expenses.
programmes.source_label: Department of Justice, 2026–2030 capital plan

programmes.title: Courts capital programme
programmes.description: The justice capital programme allocates €71.5 million to the Courts Service's physical and other capital needs in 2026.
programmes.limitation: This is distinct from court operations, legal aid and judicial salaries.
programmes.source_label: Department of Justice, 2026–2030 capital plan

programmes.title: Garda staff pay budget
programmes.description: The Garda Annual Service Plan reports a €1.48 billion 2026 pay budget supporting policing and related staff costs.
programmes.limitation: This is the staff pay line, not the total Garda budget or total justice spending.
programmes.source_label: An Garda Síochána Annual Service Plan 2026

programmes.title: Garda pensions and gratuities
programmes.description: The 2026 Garda Annual Service Plan reports a €472 million pension and gratuity budget within the Garda funding picture.
programmes.limitation: Pensions and gratuities are distinct from the Garda employee pay budget.
programmes.source_label: An Garda Síochána Annual Service Plan 2026

programmes.title: Garda non-pay operations
programmes.description: Non-pay Garda current funding covers operating expenses, services, equipment maintenance and related operational costs.
programmes.limitation: This is not the same as Garda payroll or the Garda capital envelope.
programmes.source_label: An Garda Síochána Annual Service Plan 2026

programmes.title: Specialist disability services
programmes.description: Budget 2026 provided approximately €3.83 billion to specialist disability services delivered through the HSE and partner organisations. Its administrative home is the Department of Children, Disability and Equality.
programmes.limitation: This is distinct from disability-related income support paid under Social Protection, and the two should not be combined as one programme.
programmes.source_label: Department of Children, Disability and Equality, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Residential disability services
programmes.description: The disability budget earmarked €2.21 billion for residential support for more than 9,000 disabled people in 2026.
programmes.limitation: Residential spending is within the specialist disability-services allocation, not an additional budget.
programmes.source_label: Department of Children, Disability and Equality, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Early learning and childcare
programmes.description: Budget 2026 allocated €1.48 billion to early learning and childcare supports, including affordability, inclusion, workforce measures and delivery.
programmes.limitation: This is a department programme allocation; it does not mean every child receives an identical public subsidy.
programmes.source_label: Department of Children, Disability and Equality, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Tusla child protection and welfare
programmes.description: Tusla's Budget 2026 current funding was reported at €1.336 billion for child protection, family support and services.
programmes.limitation: The same announcement separately lists €35 million capital funding; the figure here is current funding only.
programmes.source_label: Department of Children, Disability and Equality, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Tusla residential care placements
programmes.description: A €286 million allocation supports residential care placements for children needing such services and additional capacity.
programmes.limitation: This programme is within Tusla's wider funding; it must not be added as if separate.
programmes.source_label: Department of Children, Disability and Equality, Budget 2026

programmes.title: Agriculture, food and marine budget
programmes.description: The Budget 2026 statement announced roughly €2.3 billion for the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine, supporting several farm and food-sector programmes.
programmes.limitation: This is a department-level budget announcement; it is not the entire Additional Departments sector.
programmes.source_label: Minister for Public Expenditure, Budget 2026 statement

programmes.title: ACRES agri-environment scheme
programmes.description: Budget 2026 increased funding for the ACRES environmental farming scheme to €280 million, supporting participating farmers and environmental measures.
programmes.limitation: This is within the broader agriculture allocation; the €20m increase is not in addition to the €280m total.
programmes.source_label: Minister for Public Expenditure, Budget 2026 statement

programmes.title: National Sheep Welfare Scheme
programmes.description: The Budget 2026 statement allocated €20 million to continue the National Sheep Welfare Scheme for participating farmers.
programmes.limitation: The scheme amount sits within agriculture funding and should not be added on top of the departmental total.
programmes.source_label: Minister for Public Expenditure, Budget 2026 statement

programmes.title: Ireland's EU Budget contribution
programmes.description: The Department of Finance projected approximately €4.4 billion in Ireland's contribution to the EU Budget for 2026 as part of non-voted Exchequer expenditure.
programmes.limitation: This is a forecast in the October 2026 fiscal outlook, not a final EU remittance account.
programmes.source_label: Department of Finance, Budget 2027 fiscal outlook for 2026

programmes.title: National debt interest payments
programmes.description: The 2026 fiscal outlook projected roughly €2.7 billion of national debt interest payments as one component of non-voted expenditure.
programmes.limitation: Do not confuse cash debt-interest payments with principal repayments, ESA-style interest, or the entire non-voted spending category.
programmes.source_label: Department of Finance, Budget 2027 fiscal outlook for 2026

programmes.title: Future Ireland Fund transfer
programmes.description: The Department of Finance projected a €4.5 billion contribution to the Future Ireland Fund in 2026 as part of non-voted spending.
programmes.limitation: This is a transfer into a State investment fund, not a claim that this amount was spent delivering public services in 2026.
programmes.source_label: Department of Finance, Budget 2027 fiscal outlook for 2026

programmes.title: Infrastructure, Climate and Nature Fund transfer
programmes.description: The Department of Finance projected a €2 billion contribution to the Infrastructure, Climate and Nature Fund for 2026 as a central fund transfer.
programmes.limitation: An allocation into a fund is not the same as capital expenditure on an individual climate or infrastructure project.
programmes.source_label: Department of Finance, Budget 2027 fiscal outlook for 2026
